title: What is Azure
description: Learn what Azure is, how cloud computing works for developers, and the difference between IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS.

data.text: **Microsoft Azure** is a cloud computing platform and service created by Microsoft. It provides a wide range of services — from simple storage to powerful artificial intelligence — that developers use to build, deploy, and manage applications through Microsoft's global network of data centers.

Instead of buying and maintaining physical servers, developers can rent computing power, storage, and services from Azure. This means you can focus on writing code rather than managing hardware. Azure handles the underlying infrastructure, and you pay only for what you use.

data.title: Benefits for Developers
items: **No hardware to manage** — Azure runs your apps on its servers
**Scale on demand** — Add more power when traffic increases, scale down when it drops
**Pay-as-you-go** — You only pay for the resources you actually consume
**Global reach** — Deploy apps close to users worldwide
**Built-in services** — Databases, AI, storage, and networking are available with a few clicks

data.text: Azure services fall into three main categories based on how much control you have versus how much work Azure does for you.

rows: Azure App Service, Azure SQL Database

data.title: As a Developer
data.text: You will mostly use PaaS and IaaS. PaaS is great when you want Azure to handle the servers and operating system. IaaS gives you more control when you need a specific configuration.

Azure has more regions (geographic areas containing one or more data centers) than any other cloud provider. A region is a specific location, like East US or West Europe. Each region has multiple data centers for redundancy.

terms.definition: Delivering computing services over the internet so you do not need to manage physical servers yourself.
Infrastructure as a Service: you manage the operating system and apps, Azure manages the physical hardware.
Platform as a Service: Azure manages the platform, you only manage your apps and data.
Software as a Service: fully managed software delivered over the internet.
A geographic area containing one or more Azure data centers, such as East US or West Europe.

data.text: Try It: Your First Azure Resources
You can create everything in the portal, but the CLI is faster to repeat and easier to put in a script. The commands below create a resource group, an App Service plan, and a Linux web app.

data.title: Create and inspect a web app with Azure CLI
data.content: Every resource you create must belong to a resource group, and the resource group belongs to a subscription.
data.code:
# Sign in and select the subscription to use
az login
az account set --subscription "My Subscription"

# Create a resource group near your users
az group create --name rg-demo --location westeurope

# Create an App Service plan and a Linux web app
az appservice plan create \
  --name plan-demo \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --sku B1 \
  --is-linux

az webapp create \
  --name demo-app-$RANDOM \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --plan plan-demo \
  --runtime "DOTNETCORE:8.0"

# List what you created
az resource list --resource-group rg-demo --output table

data.title: Delete the resource group when you are done
data.text: Azure bills for resources while they exist, not only while they receive traffic. A single `az group delete --name rg-demo --yes` removes everything in the group, which is the fastest way to stop charges after a learning exercise.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure is Microsoft's cloud platform for building and running applications
Cloud computing removes the need to manage physical servers
IaaS gives you control over the OS; PaaS removes that burden
Azure operates across many global regions for reliability
data.takeaway: Azure lets developers deploy apps fast, scale easily, and focus on code instead of infrastructure.
